original-space.t: A ring of **arrows pointing in many directions**, all the same length. We will see what a matrix **does to every one of them**.

transform.t: The matrix **A** transforms every vector. It can change both its **direction and its length**, so the new, coloured arrows differ from the gray originals.

most-vectors-turn.t: Compare each arrow before and after. For almost every vector the **direction has turned**: the coloured arrow no longer lies along its gray original.

special-direction.t: But along **two special lines** the transformed vector lands on the **same line it started on**. These are the directions the matrix treats most simply.

eigenvector.t: A vector that **keeps its direction** under A is an **eigenvector**. It is only stretched, shrunk or flipped, never turned.

eigenvalue.h: THE SCALING FACTOR IS THE EIGENVALUE
eigenvalue.t: **A v = λ v.** Along **[1, 1]** the stretch is **λ = 3**, and along **[1, −1]** it is **λ = 1**. The eigenvalue says how much its eigenvector is stretched.

ml-connection.t: For a data covariance matrix, the eigenvectors point along the **main directions of the data**, and the eigenvalues say how much spread lies along each. **PCA uses exactly these.**
